title: Reported speech
objectives: I can report a statement with 'що', keeping the tense the speaker used and changing only the persons, where English moves every tense back.
I can report a yes or no question with 'чи' and any other question with its question word.
I can report a request or a command with 'щоб' and the past form, and tell 'сказа́в, що' from 'сказа́в, щоб'.
I can choose a precise verb of saying and show doubt about reported words with 'ні́бито' and 'мо́вляв'.
I can write direct speech in «» after a colon, and explain how 'ні́бито', 'мо́вляв' and the new verbs are spelled and said.

vocabulary.note: 'Повідо́млю', 'повідо́миш', 'повідо́млять': 'л' is added after 'м' in the 'я' and 'вони́' forms. The imperfective partner is 'повідомля́ти'. The person informed is in the accusative and the topic follows 'про': 'повідо́мити дру́зів про вечі́рку'. It is the verb of news and official notices, and the noun 'повідо́млення', message, comes from it.

example.target: Газе́та повідо́мила, що музе́й відчи́нять у тра́вні.
example.source: The newspaper reported that the museum would open in May.
example.source_literal: Newspaper informed, that museum they-will-open in May.

vocabulary.note: 'Стве́рджую', 'стве́рджуєш', like 'працюва́ти'. The perfective partner is 'стве́рдити' ('стве́рджу', 'стве́рдиш'). It reports a firm claim, often one that others doubt, so a reporter who chooses it keeps some distance from the claim.

example.target: Тара́с стве́рджує, що ніко́ли не був у Льво́ві.
example.source: Taras claims he has never been to Lviv.
example.source_literal: Taras claims, that never not was in Lviv.

vocabulary.note: 'Заявля́ю', 'заявля́єш', like 'чита́ти'. The perfective partner is 'заяви́ти' ('заявлю́', 'зая́виш'). It reports a public or official statement and is common in the news. It shares its root with 'зая́ва', a formal application.

example.target: Вла́сник заявля́є, що буди́нок не бу́дуть ремонтува́ти.
example.source: The owner states that the building will not be renovated.
example.source_literal: Owner declares, that building not they-will to-renovate.

vocabulary.note: 'Ви́словлю', 'ви́словиш', 'ви́словлять': 'л' is added after 'в' in the 'я' and 'вони́' forms. The imperfective partner is 'висло́влювати'. It takes an object, such as 'ду́мку', an opinion, rather than a clause with 'що'.

'Зізна́юся', 'зізна́єшся', like 'чита́ти' with '-ся'. The imperfective partner is 'зізнава́тися'. It reports something unpleasant that the speaker owns up to, and is followed by 'що' and a clause, or by 'в' with the locative: 'зізна́тися в по́милці', to admit a mistake. The '-ся' belongs to the verb and does not mean 'oneself'.

example.target: Сем зізна́вся, що не прочита́в кни́гу.
example.source: Sam admitted that he had not read the book.
example.source_literal: Sam admitted, that not read book.

vocabulary.note: 'Поска́ржуся', 'поска́ржишся', second conjugation. The imperfective partner is 'ска́ржитися'. The person complained to is in the dative, and what is complained about follows 'на' with the accusative or 'що' with a clause.

example.target: Оле́на поска́ржилася мені́ на галасли́вих сусі́дів.
example.source: Olena complained to me about her noisy neighbors.
example.source_literal: Olena complained to-me on noisy neighbors.

vocabulary.note: 'Пообіця́ю', 'пообіця́єш', like 'чита́ти'. It is the perfective partner of 'обіця́ти', made with the prefix 'по-'. The person promised to is in the dative. What is promised follows 'що' with the future, or an infinitive when the person who promises will do it: 'пообіця́в прийти́'.

example.target: Тара́с пообіця́в Оле́ні, що допомо́же їй.
example.source: Taras promised Olena that he would help her.
example.source_literal: Taras promised to-Olena, that will-help to-her.

vocabulary.note: 'Нага́даю', 'нага́даєш', like 'чита́ти'. The imperfective partner is 'нага́дувати'. The person reminded is in the dative. A fact follows 'що' or 'про', and something to be done follows 'щоб' with the past form.

example.target: Ма́ма нага́дала мені́, щоб я купи́в хліб.
example.source: Mom reminded me to buy bread.
example.source_literal: Mom reminded to-me, that-would I bought bread.

vocabulary.note: 'Попере́джу', 'попере́диш', 'попере́дять': 'д' becomes 'дж' in the 'я' form. The imperfective partner is 'попереджа́ти'. The person warned is in the accusative. The danger follows 'про' or 'що', and a warning not to do something takes 'щоб' with 'не' and the past form.

example.target: Окса́на попере́дила нас, що бу́де дощ.
example.source: Oksana warned us that it was going to rain.
example.source_literal: Oksana warned us, that will-be rain.

vocabulary.note: 'Перепита́ю', 'перепита́єш'. The imperfective partner is 'перепи́тувати'. The prefix 'пере-' adds 'again' to 'пита́ти'. It is what you do when you did not hear or did not believe an answer, and the question follows 'чи' or a question word.

example.target: Я перепита́в, чи конце́рт спра́вді в неді́лю.
example.source: I asked again whether the concert really was on Sunday.
example.source_literal: I asked-again, whether concert really in Sunday.

vocabulary.note: 'Розповіда́ю', 'розповіда́єш', like 'чита́ти'. The perfective partner is 'розпові́сти'. It means giving an account or telling a story, something longer than what 'сказа́ти' reports. The listener is in the dative and the topic follows 'про' with the accusative.

example.target: Бабу́ся ча́сто розповіда́є нам про своє́ ди́тинство.
example.source: Grandma often tells us about her childhood.
example.source_literal: Grandma often recounts to-us about own childhood.

vocabulary.note: The perfective partner of 'розповіда́ти', conjugated like 'відпові́сти' and 'ї́сти': 'розпові́м', 'розповіси́', 'розпові́сть', 'розповімо́', 'розповісте́', 'розповідя́ть'. Past 'розпові́в', 'розпові́ла'.

example.target: Оле́на розпові́ла мені́, як вона́ заблука́ла в лі́сі.
example.source: Olena told me how she got lost in the forest.
example.source_literal: Olena recounted to-me, how she got-lost in forest.

vocabulary.note: It marks what follows as something others say that the speaker does not vouch for. It stands before the doubtful words, or, after a verb of saying, it is used as a conjunction in the place of 'що'. It contains the particle 'би' of the conditional.

It introduces the gist of someone's words or excuse, or what their behavior seemed to say, often with a little irony. It is not an exact quotation. It comes from an old verb of saying related to 'мо́ва', language, and is set off by commas.

example.target: Тара́с не прийшо́в, мо́вляв, у ньо́го бага́то робо́ти.
example.source: Taras didn't come; he has a lot of work, he says.
example.source_literal: Taras not came, saying, at him much of-work.

vocabulary.note: Plural 'чу́тки', genitive plural 'чу́ток'. It comes from 'чу́ти', to hear: a rumor is something heard. In Ukrainian rumors walk: 'Хо́дять чу́тки, що...', rumors are going around that...

example.target: Хо́дять чу́тки, що Тара́с переї́де до Льво́ва.
example.source: Rumors are going around that Taras is moving to Lviv.
example.source_literal: Walk rumors, that Taras will-move to Lviv.

vocabulary.note: Someone's exact words, repeated from a text or a speech and written in «». The verb is 'цитува́ти' ('циту́ю'), to quote.

example.target: Я знайшо́в ціка́ву цита́ту в газе́ті.
example.source: I found an interesting quotation in the newspaper.

dialogues.title: What Iryna Petrivna said
dialogues.context: Sam was ill and missed his Ukrainian class. Oksana met his teacher, Iryna Petrivna, at the university, and now she phones Sam to pass on what the teacher said about the exam, 'і́спит'. Oksana and Sam are friends and say 'ти'.

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Се́ме, приві́т! Я сього́дні ба́чила Іри́ну Петрі́вну в університе́ті.
lines.source: Sam, hi! I saw Iryna Petrivna at the university today.
lines.source_literal: Sam, hi! I today saw Iryna Petrivna in university.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Пра́вда? І що вона́ сказа́ла?
lines.source: Really? And what did she say?
lines.source_literal: Truth? And what she said?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Споча́тку вона́ запита́ла, чи ти вже здоро́вий.
lines.source: First she asked whether you were well again.
lines.source_literal: First she asked, whether you already healthy.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Мені́ вже кра́ще. А про і́спит вона́ щось каза́ла?
lines.source: I'm feeling better now. Did she say anything about the exam?
lines.source_literal: To-me already better. And about exam she something said?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Так. Вона́ сказа́ла, що і́спит бу́де в п’я́тницю о дев’я́тій.
lines.source: Yes. She said the exam would be on Friday at nine.
lines.source_literal: Yes. She said, that exam will-be in Friday at ninth.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: У п’я́тницю? Я ду́мав, що в понеді́лок.
lines.source: On Friday? I thought it was on Monday.
lines.source_literal: In Friday? I thought, that in Monday.

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Ні, у п’я́тницю. І вона́ попере́дила, що і́спит бу́де важки́й.
lines.source: No, on Friday. And she warned that the exam would be hard.
lines.source_literal: No, in Friday. And she warned, that exam will-be hard.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: А що тре́ба повтори́ти?
lines.source: And what do I need to review?
lines.source_literal: And what needed to-review?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Вона́ сказа́ла, щоб ти повтори́в усі́ відмі́нки й ви́ди дієсло́ва.
lines.source: She said you should review all the cases and the aspects of the verb.
lines.source_literal: She said, that-would you reviewed all cases and aspects of-verb.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Чека́й, я перепита́ю. Усі́ сім відмі́нків?
lines.source: Wait, let me ask again. All seven cases?
lines.source_literal: Wait, I will-ask-again. All seven of-cases?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Так, усі́ сім. А ще вона́ проси́ла, щоб ти написа́в їй, коли́ бу́деш здоро́вий.
lines.source: Yes, all seven. She also asked you to write to her when you're well.
lines.source_literal: Yes, all seven. And also she asked, that-would you wrote to-her, when will-be healthy.

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Напишу́ сього́дні. А вона́ не сказа́ла, скі́льки бу́де пита́нь?
lines.source: I'll write today. Did she say how many questions there would be?
lines.source_literal: I-will-write today. And she not said, how-many will-be of-questions?

lines.speaker: Окса́на
lines.target: Два́дцять. Вона́ пообіця́ла, що в четве́р відпові́сть на всі ва́ші пита́ння. І ще сказа́ла: «Хай Сем не бої́ться».
lines.source: Twenty. She promised that on Thursday she would answer all your questions. And she also said, 'Sam shouldn't be afraid.'
lines.source_literal: Twenty. She promised, that in Thursday will-answer on all your questions. And also said: «Let Sam not fear».

lines.speaker: Сем
lines.target: Дя́кую, Окса́но! Скажи́ їй, що я не бою́ся.
lines.source: Thank you, Oksana! Tell her I'm not afraid.
lines.source_literal: I-thank, Oksana! Tell to-her, that I not fear.

dialogues.title: A rumor about Andrii's café
dialogues.context: Olena tells her brother Taras a rumor she has heard about Andrii's café, and then they go to the café to ask Andrii himself. Taras and Olena say 'ти' to each other and 'ви' to Andrii.

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Тара́се, ти чув? Кажу́ть, ні́бито кафе́ Андрі́я бі́льше не працюва́тиме.
lines.source: Taras, have you heard? They say Andrii's café is supposedly closing for good.
lines.source_literal: Taras, you heard? They-say, supposedly café of-Andrii more not will-work.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Що? Хто тобі́ таке́ сказа́в?
lines.source: What? Who told you that?
lines.source_literal: What? Who to-you such said?

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Со́фія. Вона́ стве́рджує, що Андрі́й поска́ржився сусі́дці, мо́вляв, ма́ло гро́шей і бага́то робо́ти.
lines.source: Sofiia. She claims Andrii complained to his neighbor that there was too little money and too much work.
lines.source_literal: Sofiia. She claims, that Andrii complained to-neighbor, saying, little of-money and much of-work.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: А Со́фія зві́дки це зна́є?
lines.source: And how does Sofiia know that?
lines.source_literal: And Sofiia from-where this knows?

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Їй розпові́ла сама́ сусі́дка. І ще вона́ ні́бито ба́чила на две́рях кафе́ оголо́шення.
lines.source: The neighbor told her herself. And she supposedly also saw a notice on the café door.
lines.source_literal: To-her recounted herself neighbor. And also she supposedly saw on door of-café notice.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: І що там напи́сано?
lines.source: And what does it say?
lines.source_literal: And what there written?

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: Со́фія ка́же, що там напи́сано: «Кафе́ зачи́нено». Бі́льше нічо́го.
lines.source: Sofiia says it says 'Café closed.' Nothing more.
lines.source_literal: Sofiia says, that there written: «Café closed». More nothing.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Це ще не означа́є, що кафе́ бі́льше не працюва́тиме. Ході́мо до Андрі́я й запита́ємо.
lines.source: That doesn't mean the café is closing for good. Let's go to Andrii and ask.
lines.source_literal: This yet not means, that café more not will-work. Let's-go to Andrii and we-will-ask.

lines.speaker: Оле́на
lines.target: До́брий день, па́не Андрі́ю! Ми чу́ли, ні́бито ви бі́льше не бу́дете працюва́ти. Це пра́вда?
lines.source: Good afternoon, Andrii! We heard that you supposedly won't be working any more. Is it true?
lines.source_literal: Good day, mister Andrii! We heard, supposedly you more not will to-work. This truth?

lines.speaker: Андрі́й
lines.target: Я? Зві́дки така́ чу́тка?
lines.source: Me? Where did that rumor come from?
lines.source_literal: I? From-where such rumor?

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: Ва́ша сусі́дка ні́бито ба́чила оголо́шення на две́рях. І вона́ ка́же, що ви поска́ржилися їй на робо́ту.
lines.source: Your neighbor supposedly saw a notice on the door. And she says you complained to her about your work.
lines.source_literal: Your neighbor supposedly saw notice on door. And she says, that you complained to-her on work.

lines.speaker: Андрі́й
lines.target: Я не ска́ржився. Я сказа́в, що в ме́не бага́то робо́ти, і це пра́вда. А на две́рях напи́сано, що кафе́ зачи́нено до понеді́лка.
lines.source: I didn't complain. I said I had a lot of work, and that's true. And the door says the café is closed until Monday.
lines.source_literal: I not complained. I said, that at me much of-work, and this truth. And on door written, that café closed until Monday.

lines.speaker: Тара́с
lines.target: О́тже, з понеді́лка все бу́де як завжди́?
lines.source: So from Monday everything will be as usual?
lines.source_literal: So, from Monday all will-be as always?

lines.speaker: Андрі́й
lines.target: Так, ми ремонту́ємо ку́хню. І скажі́ть Со́фії, щоб вона́ пита́ла мене́, а не сусі́дку.
lines.source: Yes, we're renovating the kitchen. And tell Sofiia to ask me, not the neighbor.
lines.source_literal: Yes, we renovate kitchen. And tell to-Sofiia, that-would she asked me, and not neighbor.

grammar.title: Reported statements: 'що' and the tense of the original words
grammar.explanation:
Direct speech gives someone's exact words: 'Він сказа́в: «Я працю́ю».' Reported speech, also called indirect speech, retells the same content from the point of view of the person speaking now: 'Він сказа́в, що працю́є.' A reported sentence has two parts. The reporting verb ('сказа́в', 'запита́в', 'пообіця́в') says what kind of speaking took place, and the reported clause carries the content. A clause is a group of words built around its own conjugated verb. A reported statement is joined to the reporting verb by the conjunction 'що', 'that', with a comma before it, as before the relative words of the unit on relative clauses. English often leaves out 'that' ('he said he was working'); Ukrainian writes 'що'.

The tense is the central difference from English. A tense in the Ukrainian reported clause is counted from the moment the words were spoken, not from the moment they are retold, so the clause keeps exactly the tense the speaker used:

- A present stays present: «Я працю́ю.» becomes 'Він сказа́в, що працю́є.', 'He said he was working.'
- A past stays past: «Я був у Льво́ві.» becomes 'Він сказа́в, що був у Льво́ві.', 'He said he had been in Lviv.'
- A future stays future: «Я бу́ду вдо́ма.» becomes 'Вона́ сказа́ла, що бу́де вдо́ма.', 'She said she would be at home.'

English moves every tense of a reported clause one step into the past: 'am working' becomes 'was working', 'was' becomes 'had been', 'will' becomes 'would'. This shift is called backshift, and Ukrainian has none. 'Він сказа́в, що працю́є' means that he was working at the time he spoke, and 'Він сказа́в, що працюва́в' means that he had worked before he spoke. When you translate into English, add the backshift; when you translate into Ukrainian, remove it and use the tense of the original words.

What does change is every word that points at the people in the conversation:

- The pronoun 'я' of the speaker becomes 'він' or 'вона́', and the verb ending follows: 'працю́ю' becomes 'працю́є'.
- The pronoun 'ти' and its forms, said to you, become 'я' and its forms when you retell them: «Я тебе́ чека́ю.» becomes 'Вона́ сказа́ла, що чека́є мене́.'
- Possessives follow the persons: «Мій брат живе́ в Оде́сі.» becomes 'Він сказа́в, що його́ брат живе́ в Оде́сі.'

When the subject of the reported clause is the person who spoke, it is usually left out, because the verb ending or the context shows who it is: 'Окса́на сказа́ла, що бу́де вдо́ма.' The person told is in the dative: 'Він сказа́в мені́, що...'

Words of time and place point at the moment and the place of speaking, so they change only when the report is made at another time or in another place:

- 'за́втра', tomorrow, becomes 'насту́пного дня', the next day
- 'сього́дні', today, becomes 'того́ дня', that day
- 'тут', here, becomes 'там', there

A report made on the same day keeps 'за́втра'.

rows: Він сказа́в, що був у Льво́ві.
He said he had been in Lviv.
She said she would be at home.
She said she was waiting for me.
Він сказа́в, що його́ брат живе́ в Оде́сі.
He said his brother lived in Odesa.
Він сказа́в, що насту́пного дня бу́де там.
He said he would be there the next day.

examples.target: Сем сказа́в, що живе́ в Ки́єві.
examples.source: Sam said he lived in Kyiv.
examples.source_literal: Sam said, that lives in Kyiv.

examples.target: Окса́на сказа́ла, що вже прочита́ла цю кни́гу.
examples.source: Oksana said she had already read this book.
examples.source_literal: Oksana said, that already read this book.

examples.target: Тара́с сказа́в, що за́втра бу́де працюва́ти вдо́ма.
examples.source: Taras said he would work at home tomorrow.
examples.source_literal: Taras said, that tomorrow will to-work at-home.

examples.target: Іри́на Петрі́вна сказа́ла мені́, що я до́бре говорю́ украї́нською.
examples.source: Iryna Petrivna told me that I spoke Ukrainian well.
examples.source_literal: Iryna Petrivna said to-me, that I well speak by-Ukrainian.

examples.target: Мико́ла сказа́в, що його́ до́нька живе́ в Ки́єві.
examples.source: Mykola said his daughter lived in Kyiv.
examples.source_literal: Mykola said, that his daughter lives in Kyiv.

grammar.title: Reported questions: 'чи' and the question words
grammar.explanation:
An indirect question is a question retold inside a statement: 'She asked whether I was at home.' It does not ask anything now, so it ends with a period, not a question mark. Ukrainian builds it as it builds a reported statement: a reporting verb, a comma and a clause that keeps the tense of the original question and changes only the persons.

A question that expects the answer 'так' or 'ні' has no question word. In direct speech it can be asked by intonation alone, «Ти бу́деш уве́чері вдо́ма?», or opened by the particle 'чи', «Чи ти бу́деш уве́чері вдо́ма?» In a reported question 'чи' is required, because it is the only word that shows the clause is a question. Here 'чи' works as a conjunction meaning 'whether':

- «Ти бу́деш уве́чері вдо́ма?» becomes 'Вона́ запита́ла, чи я бу́ду уве́чері вдо́ма.'
- «Ви зна́єте Тара́са?» becomes 'Сем запита́в, чи ми зна́ємо Тара́са.'

English uses 'if' both for a reported question and for a condition: 'She asked if I was at home', 'If I am at home, I'll call you.' Ukrainian keeps the two apart: 'чи' for the question, 'якщо́' or 'якби́' for the condition.

A question with a question word keeps that word at the head of the reported clause. The question words are:

- 'хто', who
- 'що', what
- 'де', where
- 'куди́', where to
- 'зві́дки', where from
- 'коли́', when
- 'чому́', why
- 'як', how
- 'скі́льки', how much or how many
- 'яки́й', which or what kind of

Such questions are reported like this:

- «Де ти живе́ш?» becomes 'Він запита́в, де я живу́.'
- «Коли́ почина́ється фільм?» becomes 'Вона́ запита́ла, коли́ почина́ється фільм.'

English has to rearrange such a question and drop 'do': 'Where do you live?' becomes 'where I lived'. A Ukrainian question has no helper word like 'do', and its word order stays the same when it is reported; only the persons change.

The verbs that report a question are:

- 'пита́ти' and its perfective 'запита́ти', to ask
- 'перепита́ти', to ask again
- the phrase 'хоті́ти зна́ти', to want to know

The person asked is in the accusative: 'Сем запита́в Окса́ну, чи...' 'Запита́ти' asks for information, while 'проси́ти' asks for a thing or an action, which the next note reports with 'щоб'. The same clauses also follow other verbs of knowing and telling: 'Я не зна́ю, чи Андрі́й сього́дні працю́є.', 'Скажи́, де ти був.'

grammar.title: Reported requests and commands: 'щоб' and the past form
grammar.explanation:
A request or a command does not state a fact; it says what the speaker wants someone to do. In direct speech it is an imperative: «Прийди́ о сьо́мій!» When it is reported, Ukrainian uses the construction of the unit on wishes and purpose: 'щоб' and the past form of the verb. 'Він сказа́в, щоб я прийшо́в о сьо́мій.' means 'He told me to come at seven.'

The past form after 'щоб' does not mean past time. 'Щоб' is 'що' with the particle 'б', the particle of the conditional, and together with the past form it presents the action as wanted, not as done. The past form agrees in gender and number with its own subject, the person who is to act, and that subject is normally named, because the past form does not show the person:

- «Прийди́ о сьо́мій!» said to a woman becomes 'Він сказа́в, щоб вона́ прийшла́ о сьо́мій.'
- «Купі́ть молоко́, будь ла́ска.» becomes 'Ма́ма проси́ла, щоб ми купи́ли молоко́.'
- A negative command keeps 'не' before the verb: «Не чека́й мене́!» becomes 'Вона́ сказа́ла, щоб я не чека́в її́.'
- A command with 'неха́й' or 'хай' about a third person is reported the same way: «Хай Сем напи́ше мені́.» becomes 'Вона́ сказа́ла, щоб Сем написа́в їй.'

English reports a command with an object and an infinitive: 'told me to come', 'asked us to buy'. Ukrainian reports it with a clause that has a subject of its own. As the unit on 'щоб' showed, 'проси́ти' can also take the person asked in the accusative and an infinitive: 'Ма́ма проси́ла нас купи́ти молоко́.' Conversation sometimes uses an infinitive after 'сказа́ти' too ('Та́то сказа́в нам почека́ти.'), but the clause with 'щоб' is the standard form and works after every verb of this kind.

One letter separates a reported statement from a reported command, so the choice between 'що' and 'щоб' decides the meaning:

- 'Він сказа́в, що я прийшо́в.' reports a fact: he said that I had come.
- 'Він сказа́в, щоб я прийшо́в.' reports a command: he told me to come.

The verbs that report a request or a command are:

- 'сказа́ти', to tell
- 'проси́ти', to ask
- 'вимага́ти', to demand
- 'наполяга́ти на то́му, щоб', to insist that
- 'нага́дати', to remind, when the reminder concerns something to be done
- 'попере́дити', to warn, when the warning concerns something to be done

A warning not to do something takes 'щоб' with 'не'. The aspect of the verb after 'щоб' is the aspect of the original imperative: one specific act is perfective ('щоб ти купи́в'), a habit or a process is imperfective ('щоб ти чита́в бі́льше').

He told her to come at seven.
Ма́ма проси́ла, щоб ми купи́ли молоко́.
Mom asked us to buy milk.
Вона́ сказа́ла, щоб я не чека́в її́.

grammar.title: Verbs of saying, 'ні́бито' and 'мо́вляв', and direct speech
grammar.explanation:
'Каза́ти' and 'сказа́ти' are the neutral verbs of saying: they report only that words were spoken. 'Розповіда́ти' and 'розпові́сти' report an account, a story with several facts. The other verbs of saying also name the kind of act the speaker performed, so choosing one tells the listener how something was said, not only what was said:

- 'повідо́мити': to inform, as news and official notices do
- 'стве́рджувати': to claim firmly, often something others doubt
- 'заявля́ти': to state publicly
- 'ви́словити': to express an opinion; it takes an object, such as 'ду́мку'
- 'зізна́тися': to admit something unpleasant
- 'поска́ржитися': to complain
- 'пообіця́ти': to promise
- 'нага́дати': to remind
- 'попере́дити': to warn
- 'перепита́ти': to ask again
- 'запере́чувати': to deny

The kind of content decides what follows the verb, as the previous notes showed: 'що' for a statement, 'чи' or a question word for a question, 'щоб' for something to be done. 'Нага́дати' and 'попере́дити' take either 'що' or 'щоб', according to whether they report a fact or an action wanted. Many of these verbs name their topic with 'про' and the accusative: 'повідо́мити про конце́рт', 'розпові́сти про по́дорож'.

A reporter who does not vouch for the words says so with a particle. 'Ні́бито' means 'supposedly' or 'allegedly'. It stands before the doubtful words ('Він ні́бито хво́рий.'), or, after a verb of saying, it is used as a conjunction in the place of 'що' and joins the two clauses: 'Він ка́же, ні́бито хво́рий.' The sentence 'Він ка́же, що хво́рий.' reports the same words without doubt. Ukrainian news uses 'ні́бито' for claims that nobody has confirmed.

'Мо́вляв' gives the gist of someone's words, or of what their behavior seemed to say, rather than an exact quotation. English renders it with 'saying that', 'as if to say' or 'he says', and it usually carries a little irony. Commas set it off: 'Він не прийшо́в, мо́вляв, у ньо́го бага́то робо́ти.' It belongs to conversation and to stories, not to official writing.

When the person who said something is unknown or unimportant, Ukrainian uses 'кажу́ть', 'they say', the 'вони́' form with no subject, as in the unit on impersonal sentences. A rumor walks in Ukrainian: 'Хо́дять чу́тки, що...', literally 'walk rumors that...'. News reports attribute a claim with 'за слова́ми' and the genitive, literally 'by words of': 'за слова́ми Богда́на', 'according to Bohdan'.

Direct speech repeats the exact words; such words taken from a text or a speech are 'цита́та'. In this course direct speech follows a colon and stands inside the Ukrainian quotation marks «», and its first word has a capital letter:

- A statement ends with a period after the closing mark: 'Він сказа́в: «Я працю́ю».'
- A question mark or an exclamation mark stays inside: 'Вона́ запита́ла: «Ти вдо́ма?»'

Ukrainian books also set out a conversation line by line, with a dash before each speaker's words; this course writes all direct speech in «».

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: ні́бито, мо́вляв, the new verbs and «»
grammar.explanation:
'Ні́бито' is written as one word and has three syllables, 'ні́-би-то', stressed on the first: [ˈnʲibɪtɔ]. The 'н' is soft before 'і', and the unstressed 'и' leans a little toward 'е', as unstressed 'и' always does. Inside it is the particle 'би' of the conditional: 'ні́би' means 'as if', and the particle 'то' follows. Like 'якби́' and 'щоб', it is one word because the particle has fused with the word before it.

'Мо́вляв' has two syllables, 'мо́в-ляв'. Both letters 'в' stand at the end of a syllable, so both are said [w], as in 'Львів': [ˈmɔwlʲɑw]. The 'л' is soft before 'я'.

The forms of several new verbs follow the rules of the earlier units:

- After 'б', 'п', 'в', 'м' and 'ф' a verb of the second conjugation adds 'л' in the 'я' and 'вони́' forms, as 'люби́ти' does in 'люблю́': 'повідо́мити', 'повідо́млю', 'повідо́млять'; 'ви́словити', 'ви́словлю'.
- In 'ви́словлю' the 'в' before 'л' ends a syllable and is said [w].
- A 'д' at the end of the stem becomes 'дж' before '-у', as in 'ходжу́': 'попере́дити', 'попере́джу'. The imperfective 'попереджа́ти' keeps 'дж' in every form, and 'стве́рджувати' has the same 'дж'. Where 'дж' stands in place of 'д' like this, it is one sound, [d͡ʒ].
- A perfective with the prefix 'ви-' is stressed on the prefix in every form: 'ви́словити', 'ви́словив', 'ви́словлю'. Its imperfective partner 'висло́влювати' is stressed on the stem.
- 'Поска́ржитися' is second conjugation, and after 'ж' the 'я' form ends in '-у', not '-ю': 'поска́ржуся', 'поска́ржишся'.
- The stress of some new verbs moves between forms, so learn it with each form. 'Розпові́сти', like 'відпові́сти', is stressed on 'ві' in 'розпові́м' and 'розпові́сть' but on the ending in 'розповіси́', 'розповімо́', 'розповісте́' and 'розповідя́ть'. 'Заяви́ти' is stressed on the ending in 'заявлю́' and on the stem in 'зая́виш' and 'зая́вить'.

The prefixes of the new verbs keep their own spelling:

- The prefix 'з-' takes the form 'зі-' before some groups of consonants, just as the preposition 'з' becomes 'зі' in 'зі шко́ли'. Before the 'зн' of 'зна́ти' it gives 'зізна́тися', with the first 'з' soft before 'і'.
- The 'з' of 'роз-' stays [z] before 'п' in 'розпові́сти' and 'розповіда́ти'. Ukrainian keeps a voiced consonant voiced before a voiceless one, apart from exceptions such as 'г' in 'легки́й'.
- 'Пообіця́ти' is 'по-' plus 'обіця́ти'. The two letters 'о' meet, and each is its own syllable, 'по-о-бі-ця́-ти', said one after the other with no consonant between them.

'Чу́тка' comes from 'чу́ти'. Its genitive plural 'чу́ток' inserts 'о' so that the word does not end in the cluster 'тк', as 'пля́шка' gives 'пля́шок'. 'Цита́та' has a hard 'ц' before 'и': [t͡sɪˈtɑtɑ].

The marks «» are called 'ла́пки', literally 'little paws'. They are written, not said; a reader shows a quotation only with a short pause and a change of voice.

culture.title: Who said it? Rumors and news
culture.text:
Ukrainians pass news on through friends, relatives and neighbors, and a story often begins with 'Кажу́ть, що...' (They say that...) or 'Хо́дять чу́тки, що...' (Rumors are going around that...). Ukrainian also has ready phrases for doubting a story:

- 'одна́ ба́ба сказа́ла', literally 'one old-woman said': a joking label for a rumor that nobody can trace, often shortened to its initials, ОБС
- 'Каза́ла На́стя, як уда́сться', literally 'said Nastia, as it-will-turn-out': a rhyming saying for a plan whose outcome nobody can promise, where 'На́стя' is a woman's name
- 'Хто це сказа́в?': 'Who said that?', the first question to ask about any rumor
- 'Зві́дки ти це зна́єш?': 'How do you know that?', literally 'from-where you this know?'

'Ба́ба' is the everyday word for an old woman, and in the countryside also for a grandmother. The joke is not unkind: it pictures the neighbor on the bench outside the building who knows everything about everyone.

Ukrainian readers pay close attention to where news comes from. In 2014 teachers and students of journalism in Kyiv founded StopFake, a project that checks news stories and quotations and shows which are false, and many other fact-checking projects followed. A careful Ukrainian news report names the source of every claim with 'за слова́ми' (according to), uses a precise verb such as 'повідо́мив' or 'заяви́в' to say who reported or stated it, and marks a claim nobody has confirmed with 'ні́бито'.

The quotation marks «» are called 'ла́пки', 'little paws'. Ukrainian uses them for every quotation, and a quotation inside a quotation takes the marks „“, as in a newspaper headline that quotes a speaker who quotes someone else.

paragraphs.target: У на́шому мі́сті збуду́ють нову́ бібліоте́ку. Про це вчо́ра повідо́мила міська́ ра́да. Бібліоте́ка бу́де на пло́щі, де за́раз працю́є стари́й ри́нок.
paragraphs.source: A new library will be built in our city. The city council announced this yesterday. The library will stand on the square where the old market is now.
paragraphs.source_literal: In our city they-will-build new library. About this yesterday informed city council. Library will-be on square, where now works old market.

paragraphs.target: Богда́н Ковале́нко з міської́ ра́ди заяви́в журналі́стам, що бібліоте́ку відчи́нять че́рез два ро́ки.
paragraphs.source: Bohdan Kovalenko of the city council told journalists that the library would open in two years.
paragraphs.source_literal: Bohdan Kovalenko from city council declared to-journalists, that library they-will-open after two years.

paragraphs.target: Він пообіця́в, що ри́нок не зачи́нять, а перене́суть на і́ншу ву́лицю бі́ля па́рку. За його́ слова́ми, продавці́ нічо́го не втра́тять.
paragraphs.source: He promised that the market would not be closed but moved to another street near the park. According to him, the sellers would lose nothing.
paragraphs.source_literal: He promised, that market not they-will-close, but they-will-carry-over to other street near park. By his words, sellers nothing not will-lose.

paragraphs.source_literal: But sellers have other opinion. One from them complained, that to-them nobody nothing not said. About library they read in newspaper.

paragraphs.target: Хо́дять і чу́тки. Ні́бито на пло́щі збуду́ють не бібліоте́ку, а готе́ль. Одна́ жі́нка, яка́ живе́ бі́ля ри́нку, стве́рджує, що ба́чила план готе́лю.

paragraphs.source_literal: Walk also rumors. Supposedly on square they-will-build not library, but hotel. One woman, who lives near market, claims, that saw plan of-hotel.

paragraphs.target: Наш журналі́ст запита́в па́на Ковале́нка, чи це пра́вда. Він відпові́в: «Ні, готе́лю не бу́де. На пло́щі бу́де бібліоте́ка».

paragraphs.source_literal: Our journalist asked mister Kovalenko, whether this truth. He answered: «No, of-hotel not will-be. On square will-be library».

paragraphs.target: Ра́да нага́дала, що в лю́тому бу́де зу́стріч для всіх, хто живе́ бі́ля пло́щі. Там ко́жен, хто хо́че, ви́словить свою́ ду́мку.
paragraphs.source: The council reminded everyone that in February there would be a meeting for all who live near the square. There anyone who wishes will give their opinion.
paragraphs.source_literal: Council reminded, that in February will-be meeting for all, who lives near square. There everyone, who wants, will-express own opinion.

That the library will be too small
That nobody had told them, and they read the news in the newspaper
questions.explanation: 'Оди́н із них поска́ржився, що їм ніхто́ нічо́го не сказа́в. Про бібліоте́ку вони́ прочита́ли в газе́ті.'

questions.prompt: Why does the report write 'Ні́бито на пло́щі збуду́ють не бібліоте́ку, а готе́ль'?
choices: The council announced a hotel instead of a library.
The newspaper passes on a rumor that it does not vouch for.
The hotel will certainly be built next to the library.
questions.explanation: 'Ні́бито' marks a claim as something said by others that the reporter has not confirmed, and the paragraph opens with 'Хо́дять і чу́тки'.

questions.prompt: The report says 'Богда́н Ковале́нко заяви́в журналі́стам, що бібліоте́ку відчи́нять че́рез два ро́ки.' Which tense did Kovalenko himself use?
choices: The past
The present
The future
questions.explanation: A Ukrainian reported clause keeps the tense of the original words, so 'відчи́нять' is the future he used. English shifts it back to 'would open'.

paragraphs.target: Мину́лого мі́сяця в кварти́ру над на́ми переї́хала нова́ сусі́дка. Ніхто́ не знав, хто вона́, але́ всі хоті́ли зна́ти.
paragraphs.source: Last month a new neighbor moved into the apartment above us. Nobody knew who she was, but everyone wanted to know.
paragraphs.source_literal: Of-last month in apartment above us moved new neighbor. Nobody not knew, who she, but all wanted to-know.

paragraphs.target: Сусі́дка з пе́ршого по́верху розпові́ла мені́, що нова́ сусі́дка приї́хала з Ха́ркова. Ні́бито вона́ бага́та й ніде́ не працю́є.
paragraphs.source: The neighbor from the first floor told me that the new neighbor had come from Kharkiv. Supposedly she was rich and did not work anywhere.
paragraphs.source_literal: Neighbor from first floor recounted to-me, that new neighbor arrived from Kharkiv. Supposedly she rich and nowhere not works.

paragraphs.target: Сусі́д із дру́гого по́верху поска́ржився, що вона́ вночі́ гра́є на гіта́рі й співа́є. Він стве́рджував, що че́рез не́ї не мо́же спа́ти.
paragraphs.source: The neighbor from the second floor complained that she played the guitar and sang at night. He claimed that he couldn't sleep because of her.
paragraphs.source_literal: Neighbor from second floor complained, that she at-night plays on guitar and sings. He claimed, that because-of her not can to-sleep.

paragraphs.target: А стари́й сусі́д із тре́тього по́верху нічо́го не розповіда́в, мо́вляв, це не його́ спра́ва.
paragraphs.source: And the old neighbor from the third floor told us nothing, as if to say it was none of his business.
paragraphs.source_literal: And old neighbor from third floor nothing not recounted, saying, this not his business.

paragraphs.target: У субо́ту я зустрі́в її́ бі́ля лі́фта й запита́в, чи вона́ спра́вді співа́є вночі́.
paragraphs.source: On Saturday I met her by the elevator and asked whether she really sang at night.
paragraphs.source_literal: In Saturday I met her near elevator and asked, whether she really sings at-night.

paragraphs.target: Вона́ розпові́ла, що працю́є в шко́лі вчи́телькою му́зики. Вона́ зізна́лася, що уве́чері і́ноді гра́є на гіта́рі, але́ вночі́ спить.
paragraphs.source: She told me that she worked at a school as a music teacher. She admitted that she sometimes played the guitar in the evening, but at night she slept.
paragraphs.source_literal: She recounted, that works in school by-teacher of-music. She admitted, that in-evening sometimes plays on guitar, but at-night sleeps.

paragraphs.target: Вона́ запита́ла, чи ми чу́ємо її́ гіта́ру. Я відпові́в, що вона́ гра́є ду́же ти́хо, і пообіця́в, що розпові́м пра́вду всім сусі́дам.
paragraphs.source: She asked whether we could hear her guitar. I answered that she played very quietly, and I promised to tell all the neighbors the truth.
paragraphs.source_literal: She asked, whether we hear her guitar. I answered, that she plays very quietly, and promised, that will-recount truth to-all neighbors.

questions.prompt: According to the neighbor from the first floor, where had the new neighbor come from?
choices: From Lviv
From Odesa
From Kharkiv
questions.explanation: 'Сусі́дка з пе́ршого по́верху розпові́ла мені́, що нова́ сусі́дка приї́хала з Ха́ркова.'

questions.prompt: What did the neighbor from the second floor complain about?
choices: That she played the guitar and sang at night
That she never said hello
That she was rich and did not work
questions.explanation: 'Сусі́д із дру́гого по́верху поска́ржився, що вона́ вночі́ гра́є на гіта́рі й співа́є.' The claim about money came from the first floor, with 'ні́бито'.

questions.prompt: What does 'мо́вляв' show in the fourth paragraph?
choices: That the old neighbor told the narrator a long story
The gist of the old neighbor's attitude, not his exact words
That the narrator agrees with the old neighbor
questions.explanation: 'Мо́вляв' gives what someone's words or silence seemed to say. The old neighbor said nothing, and 'мо́вляв, це не його́ спра́ва' sums up his attitude.

questions.prompt: What did the new neighbor admit?
choices: That she was a famous singer
That she sometimes played the guitar in the evening
That she could not sleep at night
questions.explanation: 'Вона́ зізна́лася, що уве́чері і́ноді гра́є на гіта́рі, але́ вночі́ спить.'

questions.prompt: What did the narrator promise at the end?
choices: To tell all the neighbors the truth
To learn to play the guitar
To move to another apartment
questions.explanation: 'Я пообіця́в, що розпові́м пра́вду всім сусі́дам': 'пообіця́ти' with 'що' and the future.

exercises.prompt: Match the verbs of saying with their meanings
Match the Ukrainian words with their meanings

choices: She said she was reading at home.
She said she was working at home.
She said she was resting at home.
I answered.
I complained.
I asked again.
exercises.explanation: 'Перепита́ти' is 'пита́ти' with the prefix 'пере-', which adds 'again'.

choices: попере́дити
пообіця́ти
нага́дати
зізна́тися
exercises.explanation: 'Попере́дити' is to warn. 'Пообіця́ти' is to promise, 'нага́дати' to remind and 'зізна́тися' to admit.

exercises.audio_target: Тара́с запита́в, чи ми бу́демо вдо́ма.
choices: Taras said we would be at home.
Taras asked when we would be at home.
Taras asked whether we would be at home.

exercises.prompt: What does 'Вона́ сказа́ла, щоб я прийшо́в.' mean?
choices: She said that I had come.
She told me to come.
She asked whether I had come.
exercises.explanation: 'Щоб' with the past form reports a command, so 'прийшо́в' here means the coming she wanted. 'Сказа́ла, що я прийшо́в' would report the fact that I had come.

exercises.prompt_target: Тара́с сказа́в, ___ вже прочита́в цю кни́гу.
exercises.hint_source: Taras said he had already read this book.
exercises.explanation: A reported statement is joined by 'що', and the past 'прочита́в' is the tense Taras used.

exercises.prompt_target: Він запита́в, ___ я бу́ду на вечі́рці.
exercises.hint_source: He asked whether I would be at the party.
exercises.explanation: A reported yes or no question opens with 'чи', meaning 'whether', and keeps the future of «Ти бу́деш на вечі́рці?».

exercises.prompt_target: Вона́ сказа́ла, ___ ми прийшли́ о во́сьмій.
exercises.hint_source: She told us to come at eight.
exercises.explanation: A reported command takes 'щоб' with the past form, here 'прийшли́' for 'ми'.

exercises.hint_source: Sam said he was working in the library.
exercises.explanation: Sam said «Я працю́ю», and the reported clause keeps his present tense: only the person changes, to 'працю́є'. English shifts it to 'was working'.

exercises.audio_target: Ма́ма сказа́ла, щоб ми купи́ли молоко́.
choices: Mom told us to buy milk.
Mom said we had bought milk.
Mom told us to buy cheese.

exercises.hint_source: Oksana asked when I would come.
exercises.explanation: A question with a question word keeps that word, here 'коли́', and the clause keeps the future tense of the original question.

exercises.prompt: According to Oksana in the first dialogue, when is the exam?
choices: On Monday at nine
On Thursday at nine
On Friday at nine
exercises.explanation: 'Вона́ сказа́ла, що і́спит бу́де в п’я́тницю о дев’я́тій.' Sam thought it was on Monday, and on Thursday Iryna Petrivna will answer questions.

exercises.hint_source: She asked whether I was at home.

exercises.prompt: In 'Він ка́же, ні́бито хво́рий.', what does 'ні́бито' show?
choices: That he is very ill
That the speaker does not vouch for his words
That he was ill yesterday
exercises.explanation: 'Ні́бито' takes the place of 'що' and marks the reported words as doubtful. 'Він ка́же, що хво́рий' reports the same words without doubt.

exercises.prompt_target: Андрі́й ___ нам, що кафе́ зачи́нено до понеді́лка.
exercises.hint_source: Andrii reminded us that the café was closed until Monday.
exercises.explanation: 'Нага́дати' takes the person reminded in the dative, 'нам', and a fact with 'що'.

exercises.prompt_target: Хо́дять ___, що Оле́на переї́де до Оде́си.
exercises.hint_source: Rumors are going around that Olena is moving to Odesa.
exercises.explanation: 'Хо́дять чу́тки, що...' is the fixed way to say that rumors are going around: 'чу́тки' is the plural subject of 'хо́дять'.

exercises.hint_source: They say he is supposedly very rich.
exercises.explanation: 'Ні́бито' after a verb of saying takes the place of 'що' and adds 'supposedly'.

exercises.prompt_target: Вона́ проси́ла, щоб я ___ їй уве́чері.
exercises.hint_source: She asked me to write to her in the evening.
exercises.explanation: After 'щоб' the verb is the past form, which agrees with 'я': 'написа́в' for a man, 'написа́ла' for a woman.

exercises.audio_target: Окса́на попере́дила, що за́втра бу́де сніг.
choices: Oksana promised that it would snow tomorrow.
Oksana warned that it would snow tomorrow.
Oksana warned that it would rain tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: What does the notice on the door of Andrii's café say, according to Andrii in the second dialogue?
choices: That the café is closed until Monday
That the café will not work any more
That the café needs a new owner
exercises.explanation: 'На две́рях напи́сано, що кафе́ зачи́нено до понеді́лка': the kitchen is being renovated, and the rumor was wrong.

exercises.prompt_source: She asked whether I was working.
Andrii said he had read the book.

exercises.prompt: Sam said: «Я чека́ю вчи́теля». Which sentence reports his words?
choices: Сем сказа́в, що чека́в учи́теля.
Сем запита́в, чи чека́є вчи́теля.
Сем сказа́в, що чека́є вчи́теля.
exercises.explanation: The reported clause keeps the present tense Sam used and changes only the person: 'чека́ю' becomes 'чека́є'. 'Чека́в' would report «Я чека́в», and 'запита́в, чи' reports a question.

exercises.prompt: Taras said to Oksana: «Зайди́ до ме́не о шо́стій!» Which sentence reports it?
choices: Тара́с сказа́в, що Окса́на зайшла́ до ньо́го о шо́стій.
Тара́с сказа́в, щоб Окса́на зайшла́ до ньо́го о шо́стій.
Тара́с запита́в, чи Окса́на зайшла́ до ньо́го о шо́стій.
exercises.explanation: An imperative is reported with 'щоб' and the past form, which agrees with Oksana: 'зайшла́'. 'До ме́не' becomes 'до ньо́го', because 'ме́не' meant Taras.

exercises.prompt: 'Окса́на сказа́ла, що бу́де вдо́ма.' When is Oksana to be at home?
choices: Before she said it
At the moment she said it
After she said it
exercises.explanation: A Ukrainian reported clause counts its tense from the moment the words were spoken, so the future 'бу́де' means after she spoke. English says 'she said she would be at home'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'She said she had been in Odesa'?
choices: Вона́ сказа́ла, що бу́де в Оде́сі.
Вона́ сказа́ла, що була́ в Оде́сі.
Вона́ сказа́ла, що живе́ в Оде́сі.
exercises.explanation: She said «Я була́ в Оде́сі», and the past stays past. English shifts 'was' to 'had been'.

exercises.prompt: In 'Тара́с не пішо́в у кіно́, мо́вляв, нема́є гро́шей.', what does 'мо́вляв' tell you?
choices: That the reporter has checked how much money Taras has
That Taras will go to the movies later
That the reason is Taras's own explanation, given in its gist
exercises.explanation: 'Мо́вляв' gives the gist of someone's words or excuse, usually with a little irony, not an exact quotation.

exercises.prompt: Which verb asks for a thing or an action rather than for information?
choices: запита́ти
проси́ти
перепита́ти
exercises.explanation: 'Проси́ти' asks someone for something or to do something, and is reported with 'щоб'. 'Запита́ти' and 'перепита́ти' ask for information, reported with 'чи' or a question word.

exercises.prompt: Why is there an 'л' in 'повідо́млю', the 'я' form of 'повідо́мити'?
choices: Because 'л' marks a perfective verb
Because after 'б', 'п', 'в', 'м' and 'ф' a second conjugation verb adds 'л' in the 'я' form, as in 'люблю́'
Because the stem of 'повідо́мити' ends in 'л'
exercises.explanation: After 'б', 'п', 'в', 'м' and 'ф' a verb of the second conjugation adds 'л' in the 'я' and 'вони́' forms: 'повідо́млю', 'повідо́млять', as 'ви́словити' gives 'ви́словлю'.

choices: [w], because each one ends a syllable
[ʋ], as before a vowel
The first as [ʋ] and the second as [w]
exercises.explanation: In 'мо́в-ляв' the first 'в' ends the first syllable before 'л', and the second ends the word, so both are [w], as in 'Львів'.

exercises.prompt: In direct speech after a colon, where does the period of a quoted statement go?
choices: After the closing mark »
Before the closing mark »
After the colon, before «
exercises.explanation: 'Він сказа́в: «Я працю́ю».' A question mark or an exclamation mark stays inside: 'Вона́ запита́ла: «Ти вдо́ма?»'

exercises.prompt_source: She said she was at home.
exercises.explanation: English backshifts 'am' to 'was'; Ukrainian keeps the present of her words «Я вдо́ма», with no word for 'is'.

exercises.prompt_source: He asked whether I had time.
answers: Він запита́в, чи я ма́ю час.
Він запита́в, чи є в ме́не час.
Він запита́в, чи в ме́не є час.
Він запита́в мене́, чи я ма́ю час.
Він запита́в мене́, чи є в ме́не час.
Він запита́в мене́, чи в ме́не є час.
Він пита́в, чи я ма́ю час.
Він пита́в, чи є в ме́не час.
Він пита́в, чи в ме́не є час.
Він пита́в мене́, чи я ма́ю час.
Він пита́в мене́, чи є в ме́не час.
Він пита́в мене́, чи в ме́не є час.
exercises.explanation: A yes or no question is reported with 'чи' and keeps the present of the original question.

answers: Та́то сказа́в нам, щоб ми чека́ли.
Та́то нам сказа́в, щоб ми чека́ли.
Та́то сказа́в нам, щоб ми почека́ли.
Та́то нам сказа́в, щоб ми почека́ли.
Та́то каза́в нам, щоб ми чека́ли.
Та́то нам каза́в, щоб ми чека́ли.
Та́то каза́в нам, щоб ми почека́ли.
Та́то нам каза́в, щоб ми почека́ли.
exercises.explanation: A reported command takes 'щоб' and the past form with its own subject: 'щоб ми чека́ли'.
If Taras asked «Де Окса́на?», the clause keeps the present and has no verb: 'де Окса́на'. If he asked «Де була́ Окса́на?», it keeps the past.

exercises.prompt_source: They say the café is supposedly closed.
exercises.explanation: 'Кажу́ть' with no subject is 'they say', and 'ні́бито' adds 'supposedly', either in place of 'що' or before the doubtful words.

answers: Оле́на пообіця́ла, що вона́ бу́де писа́ти.
Оле́на обіця́ла, що вона́ бу́де писа́ти.
exercises.explanation: 'Пообіця́ти' takes 'що' with the future of the original promise, «Я напишу́», or an infinitive, since Olena herself will write.
